setlist_extra.title: That's It For The Other One

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Viola Lee Blues** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls this Viola Lee a very long, ferocious jam, unlike the 1973 and 1977 versions, best played loud; Reviewer judges this the best Viola Lee on tape, though it lacks the special occasion of the Haight Street version [6][11][13]
- **The Other One** (1 other source): This is the last show featuring one of the early sets of Other One lyrics, about waking with one's head missing [2]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): Reviewer notes Bobby's funky timing on the 'Coming around' section and the lyrics specific to this era [10]
- **Viola Lee Blues Feedback** (1 review): Reviewer suggests the feedback ending followed because the guitars would be badly out of tune after the meltdown [11]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.jools.20299.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 7 songs; 33 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd68-02-02.sbd.jools.15801.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 6 songs; 46 min; rated 4.62/5 by 37 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer found the tape quality rough on two plays, yet still enjoyed how it sounded; Reviewer strummed along with The Other One and found the pitch nearly perfect, with powerful sound levels [5][12]
- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.miller.97345.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 4 songs; 33 min; rated 3.93/5 by 14 [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer describes the Crystal Ballroom as an old theater with a huge spring-loaded dance floor and a wonderful vibe [4]
- Joe Jupille searched University of Washington Daily and Seattle Post-Intelligencer papers, finding only ads for Quicksilver and the Dead on 1/26 and 1/27 [1]
- Reviewer says this music appears in plainer form than the swirling studio collage of Anthem of the Sun [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.jools.20299.sbeok.shnf**: This tape circulates mislabeled as 1/23/68 Eagles Auditorium, though no evidence shows any shows there beyond 1/26 and 1/27 [1]
- **gd68-02-02.sbd.jools.15801.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Julian (Jools) Elliott; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: David Gans aired both the 2/2/68 and 2/3/68 shows on The Grateful Dead Hour soon after they surfaced; The circulating Schoolgirl is actually from 2/3/68, spliced in by David Gans for Grateful Dead Hour 310 [2][7]
- **gd1968-02-02.sbd.miller.97345.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by George Hunter: [Grateful Dead Quicksilver NOTICE! 1968 Crystal Ballroom AOR 3.103 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/374636/Grateful-Dead-Quicksilver-NOTICE-1968-Crystal-Ballroom-AOR-3103-Concert-Poster) [17]
- Fan art by jeffersonboots.free.fr: [Grateful Dead](http://jeffersonboots.free.fr/dead/dead.htm) [18]
